    - heading "Accessibility" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: "Markers and chips are buttons named \"Source 2: Latency Notes – title\", with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the preview"
      - listitem: Focusing a marker or chip lights up the same sentences and chip as hovering does
      - listitem: The preview is a named region; while closed it is inert
      - listitem: The last row of the card is announced politely – what you point at, and "Quote copied"
    - heading "Motion" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: Hovering a marker gives its sentence a soft tint and lights up its chip; hovering a chip tints every sentence that cites it and fades the rest of the answer
      - listitem: The preview unfolds below the source chips and folds away again; switching to another source crossfades its content in place
      - listitem: "The line in the last row crossfades: the old line fades out underneath while the new one fades in"
      - listitem: With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement
    - heading "Responsive behavior" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: Fills its container up to 460px and works from 300px. The source chips stay on one line – whatever doesn't fit goes into "+N", which shows them all. Below 400px the card gets tighter, below 360px the preview drops its number tag, below 280px Copy quote keeps only its icon
      - listitem: "Touch screens: larger hit areas around the markers and taller chips and buttons"
      - listitem: "Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme=\"dark\""
    - heading "Notes for AI" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Give your coding assistant this summary instead of screenshots.
    - list:
      - listitem: Numbers come from the order of sources, not from the text – cite by id, and reorder sources to renumber
      - listitem: The last word of a cited sentence stays on the line with its markers, so a marker never starts a line on its own
      - listitem: Ids in cite that aren't in sources are skipped, so a hallucinated citation never shows a broken marker
      - listitem: Without highlight, words of five letters or more (and numbers) that the quote shares with its citing sentences are marked – pass highlight for exact phrases
      - listitem: The component doesn't fetch pages – quote should be the passage your retrieval step actually used
